subject: literature
passage: Every morning that spring, old Stavros carried a bucket of water up the hill to the olive sapling he had planted at the edge of his field. His neighbor laughed and pointed out that an olive tree can take many years to bear a full crop. Stavros only shrugged and nodded toward his granddaughter, who was chasing a goat through the tall grass. "The olives are not for me," he said. "They are for her."
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Stavros's granddaughter helps him water the olive sapling each morning.
choices.B: Stavros's neighbor persuades him that planting an olive tree is a waste of time.
choices.C: Stavros worries that his young olive tree will not survive the dry spring.
choices.D: Stavros tends a tree whose harvest he expects his granddaughter to enjoy.

explanation.why: The neighbor points out that an olive tree takes many years to produce a full crop. Stavros is not bothered: he nods toward his granddaughter and says, "The olives are not for me. . . . They are for her." The main idea is that he is caring for the tree for her future benefit.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The granddaughter is chasing a goat; the text says Stavros carries the water himself.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Stavros only shrugs at his neighbor and keeps caring for the tree, so he is not persuaded.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text never says Stavros worries about the tree surviving.
explanation.D: Correct. Stavros keeps watering the sapling even though it will take years to bear fruit, because the olives are "for her."
